title: K-Means on 2D data
instruction:
Apply K-Means with k=2 to the following 2D data. Print the cluster labels for each point and the coordinates of the centroids.

Data:
[[1, 2], [1.5, 1.8], [2, 2.5], [5, 6], [5.5, 5.5], [6, 6.2]]
starter_code:
import numpy as np
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans

X = np.array([[1, 2], [1.5, 1.8], [2, 2.5], [5, 6], [5.5, 5.5], [6, 6.2]])

# Apply K-Means with k=2
solution_code:
import numpy as np
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans

X = np.array([[1, 2], [1.5, 1.8], [2, 2.5], [5, 6], [5.5, 5.5], [6, 6.2]])

kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=2, random_state=42, n_init=10)
kmeans.fit(X)
print("Labels:", kmeans.labels_)
print("Centroids:", kmeans.cluster_centers_)

title: Predict cluster for a new point
instruction: Using the same data and k=2 from the previous exercise, predict which cluster a new point [3, 4] belongs to and print the predicted cluster label.
starter_code:
import numpy as np
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans

X = np.array([[1, 2], [1.5, 1.8], [2, 2.5], [5, 6], [5.5, 5.5], [6, 6.2]])
new_point = np.array([[3, 4]])

# Train K-Means and predict
solution_code:
import numpy as np
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans

X = np.array([[1, 2], [1.5, 1.8], [2, 2.5], [5, 6], [5.5, 5.5], [6, 6.2]])
new_point = np.array([[3, 4]])

kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=2, random_state=42, n_init=10)
kmeans.fit(X)
pred = kmeans.predict(new_point)
print(pred[0])
